### kms-account-principal-delegates-to-iam

**Claim.** When the principal in a key policy statement is the account principal, the statement gives no IAM principal permission itself; it lets the account delegate the permissions with IAM policies.

> — [Default key policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-default.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### kms-asymmetric-for-outside-aws-users

### kms-client-vs-server-side-encryption

**Claim.** Server-side encryption is done by the service that receives the data; with client-side encryption, data is encrypted locally before the service receives it and the service plays no role in encrypting or decrypting it.

**Write it as.** `encrypting data locally` · `does not play a role in encrypting`

> "Server-side encryption is the act of encrypting data at its destination, by the application or service that receives it and owns the security of its storage layer."

> "Client-side encryption is the act of encrypting data locally before the target application or service receives it. The AWS service receives encrypted data; it does not play a role in encrypting or decrypting it."
> — [General encryption best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/encryption-best-practices/general-encryption-best-practices.html)

### kms-unusable-key-data-keys-delayed-effect

**Claim.** When a KMS key becomes unusable, cryptographic requests with it fail almost at once, but the effect on data keys it encrypted, and on data they encrypt, is delayed until the KMS key is used again, for example to decrypt a data key.

> "However, the effect on data keys encrypted by the KMS key, and on data encrypted by the data key, is delayed until the KMS key is used again, such as to decrypt the data key."
> — [How unusable KMS keys affect data keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/unusable-kms-keys.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### kms-unusable-key-ebs-attach-fails

**Claim.** Making a KMS key unusable has no immediate effect on an attached encrypted EBS volume, but after the volume is detached, the next attachment fails because EBS cannot decrypt the volume's data key.

**Write it as.** `no immediate effect on the EC2 instance` · `the attachment fails`

> "The next time the encrypted EBS volume is attached to an EC2 instance, the attachment fails, because Amazon EBS cannot use the KMS key to decrypt the volume's encrypted data key."

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
